item.title: ERSOY: Your liver’s cholesterol thermostat: What it really does (and what actually changes ldl)
item.description: Cholesterol is a waxy, fat-like substance your body needs to function. It’s a building block for every cell membrane, it helps your body make steroid hormones (like estrogen and testosterone), it’s used to produce vitamin D, and it’s required to form bile acids that help you digest and absorb fats.

item.title: Blessing held for Kapaa Refuse Transfer Station
item.description: KAPAA — The Department of Public Works Solid Waste Division held a blessing Friday to commemorate the first phase of renovations at the Kapaa Refuse Transfer Station.

item.title: Pacific leaders gather in Hawaii for business summit
item.description: Leaders from Pacific Island nations and territories gathered this week at the East-West Center in Manoa for an inaugural diplomatic and business summit aimed at promoting private sector investments and contracts across island communities in Oceania.

item.title: Tax preparers busy at Kalukalu
item.description: KAPAA — Business for the AARP Tax-Aide crew was brisk on Friday at the Kalukalu, or Kapaa Branch of the Kauai Community Federal Credit Union.

item.title: U.S.-Iran strikes unleash travel chaos as airlines cancel flights

item.title: War powers votes unlikely to rein in Trump after Iran strikes
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. — Lawmakers who oppose President Donald Trump’s military campaign against Iran will have a chance to weigh in next week, but they may not be able to successfully rein him in.

item.title: Trump, the self-declared peace president, goes to war seeking regime change
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. — When he first ran for president in 2016, Donald Trump disavowed the military adventurism of recent years, declaring that “regime change is a proven, absolute failure.” He promised to “stop racing to topple foreign regimes.”

item.title: Road closures for the week of February 28 – March 6
item.description: LIHUE — A number of road-related projects are on tap in the days ahead with grass cutting, tree trimming and guardrail repair making up the bulk of the work, the Hawaii Department of Transportation said in an update on Friday.
